text.p: Families of 78 people crushed to death in Guatemala's largest soccer stadium last year tried to block the reopening of the facility on Thursday.
Sports authorities hope to get permission this week from the International Football Federation (FIFA) to reopen the stadium April 16-27 for a Central American soccer cup.

"We asked the judge to block the opening of the stadium and to keep it closed until the family members have been compensated," said Rene Cordoba, a lawyer for the relatives. He said authorities wanted to invest money in reopening the Mateo Flores stadium but had ignored compensation claims.

Some 78 people were crushed to death on Oct. 16 when overcrowding triggered a human avalanche in the stadium's cement bleachers half an hour before the kickoff at a World Cup qualifying match between Costa Rica and Guatemala.
FIFA closed the stadium until changes were made to ensure the safety of fans. The Guatemalan Football Federation said on Wednesday it had made all the recommended improvements.

Criminal charges of negligence have been filed against 18 managers and employees accused of overcrowding the stadium, and families of the victims are seeking damages in more than 40 civil cases against the government and stadium management.
Investigators say 60,000 people, including 45,000 ticket holders, unticketed children and gate crashers, were packed into the stadium, which has a capacity of 32,676.
